crime_highlights: The appellant came through a rear door of a home, entered a bedroom where the female complainant was asleep
in his dealings with the complainant he threatened to use a weapon
He had cut a phone line in the house
She had earlier tried to get out of the house but had been restrained from doing so by the appellant.
It is clear from a victim impact statement that the assault had a serious effect on the complainant, who thereafter was fearful for her safety
rationale_highlights: This young appellant, who has also had alcohol problems, has an aboriginal background.
a most unfortunate background, marred by violence and drinking by his caregivers when he was a child
Substantially based on the particular circumstances of this young aboriginal offender, I would substitute for the sentence of 6 years a sentence of 4 years.
note: Brief reasoning; reduction tied to aboriginal circumstances in para 10.

crime_highlights: Mr. Reid assaulted S.R. with a knife, apparently because he was angry with her for associating with other men
Mr. Reid striking and kicking the victim and stabbing her three times with knife
All of the wounds required stitches.
he threatened her with further harm if she implicated Mr. Reid in the assault
rationale_highlights: the sentencing of aboriginal offenders must proceed on an individual (or a case-by-case) basis
What combination of systemic or background factors contributed to this particular offender coming before the courts for this particular offence?

the new information available to this Court, when considered in light of the principles expressed in such cases as Gladue, Wells and Proulx, justifies the court in finding that a term of imprisonment in excess of two years is not required to meet the factors of sentencing
note: Appeal court; Gladue discussed mainly as procedure and fresh evidence on community supports.

crime_highlights: the accused launched, apparently without any kind of provocation, an attack upon Barker with a table leg
he did succeed in causing extremely serious injuries
The bone was driven into the eye of Barker who had to have serious surgery
He told the clerk that he was there to rob him
He assaulted the clerk in a similar way
rationale_highlights: It is difficult to imagine that any judge could have more fully considered the particular aspects of this aboriginal person's difficulties and the degree of restraint shown was surely very high.
He sought to balance that with rehabilitation, with careful regard to aboriginal status.
note: Appeal court reviews trial judge's Gladue treatment; offender history is in para 6, not included.
